blocks.title: dbx-pro — a database workbench inside Astravia
blocks.description: Manage connections, browse schemas, write SQL and read editable result grids without leaving Astravia. SQLite works out of the box; the connection picker lists 85 database types with their current support tier clearly marked.

items.title: Connection manager
items.description: Keep local connection profiles with host, port, database and environment labels, and pick the type from an 85-entry catalog.

items.title: SQL editor + result grid
items.description: Multi-tab editing, one keyboard shortcut to run, and results in a sortable row grid with the row count and duration.

items.title: Table browser
items.description: Explore the schema tree, describe columns with types and keys, and preview sample rows.

items.title: Write safety gate
items.description: Connections marked as production keep writes and DDL behind an explicit release switch.

items.title: Support tiers, stated honestly
items.description: Every type shows whether it is directly queryable, experimental, or not reachable yet — no silent failures.

items.title: Open the workbench
items.description: Install dbx-pro from the marketplace and open its activity tab. Nothing else to install.

items.title: Add a connection
items.description: Pick SQLite and choose a database file to query straight away; other types are saved as profiles you can revisit.

items.title: Run a query
items.description: Type SQL and press ⌘/Ctrl+Enter to execute.

blocks.content: Only SQLite is directly queryable today. PostgreSQL, MySQL, ClickHouse and other listed types appear in the picker with their support tier, and are progressively connected through plugin drivers.
